title: Greaves wins at Le Castellet after Jota's drive-time penalty
dek: Greaves Motorsport's Hirsch, Wirdheim and Lancaster were declared winners of the 4 Hours of Le Castellet when Jota's first-on-the-road Gibson received a 45-second penalty, cutting Jota's title lead to one point.

chapters.title: Jota arrives as the points leader
text: The 4 Hours of Le Castellet on 6 September 2015 was the penultimate round of the European Le Mans Series, and the LMP2 title fight was tight enough to make it feel like a final. Jota Sport arrived leading with 60 points, two clear of Thiriet by TDS Racing, with Greaves Motorsport a further eight back. Krohn Racing sat fourth, 28 points off the lead, and Murphy Prototypes, always quick at Paul Ricard, six behind them. A winning Jota would take a firm grip; anything else would push the decision to Estoril.

The paddock news started with the team at the top. On the Friday Jota announced a full-season FIA WEC programme for 2016 with an Oreca 05 Nissan, while confirming that its Gibson 015S would stay in the ELMS for a fifth consecutive season for Simon Dolan. The entry itself shrank to twelve LMP2 cars after the two Ibanez Racing Oreca 03Rs were withdrawn. The pair of SMP Racing BR01s reappeared as AF Racing entries numbered #20 and #21 and, free of the sanctions that had prevented a contract with Goodyear-owned Dunlop, switched from Michelin to Dunlop tyres. Krohn's #40 Ligier had Olivier Pla back alongside Tracy Krohn and Niclas Jönsson, while Richard Bradley, fresh from Le Mans class victory, joined Nico Pieter de Bruijn in the Eurasia Oreca #33.

On track, teams ran Dunlop's medium and medium-plus compounds, a combination chosen for the first time that weekend. Aleshin's AF Racing BR01 led the first practice on a 1:47.986, then Tristan Gommendy topped the afternoon session in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca 05 with a 1:47.546, a strong mistral wind helping the straight-line speeds.

chapters.title: Tincknell on pole, AF Racing alongside
text: Harry Tincknell took Jota's pole in the 20-minute session with a 1:46.917 in the Gibson 015S, his third pole of the season. It was far from comfortable. The AF Racing BR01s were visibly quicker than before on Dunlops, and Nicolas Minassian put the #20 car within 0.148 seconds of the Englishman, the veteran saying he had set the car up for speed rather than comfort and wanted to win now. Race control also announced that two of Tincknell's laps, including the pole lap, were under investigation, but the time stood.

Mikhail Aleshin in the #21 BR01 was on a threatening lap but lost out in the final sector, ending 0.581 seconds adrift on 1:47.498 and third on the grid, giving the car its best qualifying result of the year. Gommendy was fourth in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca 05 on 1:47.641 after going out early and not stringing together a clean lap, with the team opting for a higher-downforce set-up. Léo Roussel was a notable fifth for Pegasus in the Morgan, ahead of Nathanaël Berthon's Murphy Oreca 03R, the pole-sitter here a year earlier, in sixth. Eurasia was seventh, and Jon Lancaster qualified the Greaves Gibson only eighth on 1:49.101, well down on the Jota. Algarve Pro Racing's Ligier was ninth and Krohn's Judd-powered Ligier tenth.

chapters.title: Aleshin leads as Jota is swamped
text: The race started at 13:00 and Jota's pole advantage was gone almost at once. Dolan, starting the #38, was swamped by both AF Racing BR01s and by Roussel's Pegasus Morgan. Aleshin took the lead at the first corner, with Roussel second and Minassian harrying him until the #20 car got through after about fifteen minutes. Aleshin then opened a gap of roughly five seconds to his team-mate, while Dolan settled into fourth and began to pressure the Morgan.

The order changed when the first Safety Car came out after around 70 minutes to retrieve the stranded Team LNT Ginetta #2, which had stopped with a technical problem. Dolan gained about twenty seconds on the leaders as the GT cars were bunched up between the groups, but he then ran wide on worn tyres and spun at Turn 2 while defending against Gary Hirsch's Greaves Gibson, losing around twelve seconds. Ludovic Badey in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca had already made an unscheduled stop with a left-rear puncture, and the car was now out of sequence with the rest.

chapters.title: Albuquerque hunts, Murphy crashes
text: Filipe Albuquerque took over the Jota after the first stint change-overs and the race swung back towards the Gibson. A second Safety Car arrived shortly after, when Michael Lyons crashed the Murphy Oreca heavily on the entry to Signes, ending its race after 61 laps. Lyons was checked at the medical centre and emerged with a bruised leg and a sore neck. The restart bunched the field again, and Albuquerque quickly passed Hirsch on the Mistral straight before reeling in Gommendy, who was leading on the road in the Thiriet by TDS car.

With Jota calling Albuquerque in for his penultimate stop with about 90 minutes left, the Portuguese was already cutting into the French car's advantage. Behind them, AF Racing's two BR01s ran comfortably in the top positions after the first Safety Car shake-out, while track limits and incidents kept the stewards busy all afternoon.

chapters.title: A three-way scrap for the podium
text: With 70 minutes left Gommendy handed over to Pierre Thiriet and the #38 Jota gained a lead of 17 seconds over Victor Shaytar's #21 AF Racing, with Thiriet emerging from the pits right on the Russian's rear wing. The pair fought over several laps, which let Lancaster close in for Greaves. Around 50 minutes from the end he made what was described as the move of the race, passing Thiriet around the outside of Turn 11, and a few corners later he dispatched Shaytar as well, pushing the AF Racing car down to fourth before it pitted for Kirill Ladygin's final stint.

Jota's 20-second lead was trimmed to 14 seconds before its last stop, when Tincknell took over on fresh tyres with about 45 minutes remaining. Lancaster's own fuel-only stop was complicated when an SVK by Speed Factory LMP3 car pitted at the same time and temporarily blocked his Greaves in, costing seconds. Thiriet's challenge then ended: the Oreca needed a long late stop for a brake problem with a suspected fluid leak and fell out of contention.

chapters.title: Jota first across the line, Greaves the winner
text: Once Tincknell was on fresh Dunlops the finish was simple. He was able to back off considerably in the closing ten minutes and took the chequered flag 30.290 seconds ahead of Lancaster's Greaves Gibson, with Ladygin's AF Racing BR01 third on the road, 35.459 seconds behind. Lancaster had needed to defend on older tyres from Ladygin in the final half hour and held on. Jota celebrated what looked like a critical victory and an 18-point lead with 26 left to win.

The celebration was short. Two and a half hours after the flag the stewards gave the #38 a 45-second time penalty for Albuquerque exceeding the maximum 90-minute drive time, by 1 minute 57 seconds. That turned Jota's victory into third place and handed the win to Greaves Motorsport's Hirsch, Bjorn Wirdheim and Lancaster, who finished 14.710 seconds ahead of the Jota on the revised result. Aleshin, Ladygin and Shaytar took second for AF Racing, 5.169 seconds behind the winners, and Minassian, Mediani and Markozov were fourth, 46 seconds behind in the other BR01. Aleshin also set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:49.769.

Behind the leaders, Krohn Racing took fifth with Pla in the closing stint the fastest man on track in the last half hour, and Thiriet by TDS came home sixth, a lap down, after what had threatened to be a winning run. Pegasus was seventh, two laps down after a puncture in the penultimate hour, and Algarve Pro Racing eighth. The Eurasia Oreca, delayed early, and the Murphy car were not classified.

chapters.title: A single point in it before Estoril
text: The revised result shook up the championship. Before the penalty Jota had left Paul Ricard 18 points clear; afterwards it led Greaves by a single point, with Thiriet by TDS slipping back to third after its brake trouble. With 26 points still available at the finale, Jota, Greaves and Thiriet by TDS went into the last round with a genuine three-way fight for the LMP2 title.

The penalty itself was a reminder of how close the margins were: Albuquerque had gone over the permitted drive time by less than two minutes, but the sanction was 45 seconds, enough to erase a 30-second victory. It was a bitter blow for Jota, who had also taken pole, and a windfall for Greaves, whose Gibson had been outpaced in qualifying and had started eighth.

AF Racing could take consolation from the best result so far for the new BR01, which had shown both speed and reliability on its first weekend on Dunlop tyres, and the team's designer and project co-ordinator were delighted with the breakthrough. Track limits, with the paved run-off areas at Paul Ricard, proved a headache for drivers and stewards alike, with plenty of penalties for exceeding them over the weekend.
The ELMS also used the weekend to unveil a six-round 2016 calendar with Spa-Francorchamps added. The season finale, the 4 Hours of Estoril, was scheduled for 18 October.

facts.v: Harry Tincknell's 1:46.917 put the Jota Gibson on pole, only 0.148 seconds ahead of Nicolas Minassian's AF Racing BR01.
